prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active forms, which made incretin-based therapy of type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part prize on B036 for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, with a citation framed around the physiology of GLP-1 and its active forms. The scientific case is the most complete on the shortlist: proglucagon processing and the identification of the active peptide, human incretin physiology, mechanisms of action in gut, pancreas and brain, and then approved therapies whose benefit on glycaemia, weight and cardiovascular and renal outcomes has been confirmed in independent randomized trials. Nobody has raised a maturity question, and none is warranted. I would keep the prize to one part. Round 1 showed no one arguing for a second part on its merits, and a second part is only worth adding if it is clearly as strong as the first. With the three-person limit, a GLP-1 trio leaves no room for a two-person B006 pair, so a second part would force a reduction of B036 that I do not think is defensible. The chair's question about the third slot is the one that matters. My answer is that the criterion should be the discovery of what the hormone is and which form is active, and by that criterion Mojsov is the better third name than Knudsen. The therapeutic consequence is recorded in the citation wording.
statement.case_against: The attribution remains imperfect and I should say so plainly. Habener is outside the supplied credit and has, on the account of every member, a real claim to the early peptide work. The citation wording cannot repair that, and I think the deliberation record should state it openly instead of implying a complete allocation. Mojsov's priority on the active peptide is contested, and none of us has checked it against the supplied evidence, so my preference for her over Knudsen rests on a judgment about the criterion more than on settled facts. If the committee concludes that the decisive achievement is the engineered long-acting agonists, the right replacement is Knudsen for Mojsov, not a fourth name. A physiology trio also risks looking as though it under-credits the development that actually reached patients.

responses.point: Linnarsson moved from Knudsen to Mojsov after reading colleagues, but says the Knudsen version would be better if the committee values the transformation of care as much as the discovery. Linnarsson also asked why I ranked imatinib (B026) above B006 and B047 in my opening.
responses.response: Your move to the physiology trio matches my own view, and I accept your caveat as a fair statement of the risk. On B026, I will not defend the opening order. Your objection and the other responses to it identify the same gap I noted myself: the BCR-ABL fusion and oncogene discoveries and the chemistry of imatinib lie outside Druker, Lydon and Sawyers. That is a development-and-proof-of-principle prize resting on uncredited foundations. I would put it below B006 and B042 in my alternatives, and I have dropped it from my list. On the third-slot question, if the committee finds that Mojsov's priority cannot be supported, I would go to Knudsen, as I said in round 1. I would not leave the slot to a name I could not justify.

responses.point: El-Manira argues that if the foundational discoveries lie outside the credited names, B026 rewards development rather than discovery. That is the same framing objection he raises against a Knudsen-based GLP-1 prize, and he says the committee must settle the principle before accepting it in one place and rejecting it in the other.
responses.response: I agree that consistency is the point, and I have changed my position as a result. I will not apply a lenient reading to imatinib and a strict one to GLP-1. The difference I would defend is that in B036 the credited discovery side, Holst, Mojsov and Drucker, covers the hormone's biology and active form, and the drug engineering is the part that would be acknowledged in the citation but not named. In B026 the credited names are all on the development side. That is why the discovery-first principle supports my B036 configuration and counts against B026. I also accept the corollary: Habener's absence from B036 is a gap in the discovery side too, so I am not claiming that GLP-1 is free of the problem. I am claiming it is smaller than for the BCR-ABL trio.

responses.point: Sandberg moved to the Drucker, Holst and Mojsov trio, and asks how a B026 set would handle the Rowley and Witte contributions. Sandberg also notes that unanimity on B036 says nothing about the ordering of the remaining candidates and that the second part is undecided.
responses.response: On Rowley and Witte, I cannot handle them within three names drawn from the supplied credit, and I no longer think B026 should take a second slot. Your second point is correct and I take it seriously. The unanimous first place on B036 gives no information about what comes next, so I am not treating it as support for any second part. My reasoning for a single part is that no second candidate has yet been shown to be as strong as B036 on both discovery and maturity. B042 is mature and widely validated but has six credited names for a methods contribution. B006 is conceptually clean but its clinical impact is still developing. I keep both as alternatives and not as a co-prize.

responses.point: Perlmann notes that B006 with Mori and Walter cannot be combined with a three-person B036 under the three-person limit, and asks that Habener's absence be noted in the citation wording. Perlmann also says B026 skips the foundational step and ranks below B006.
responses.response: I agree on the arithmetic. A two-name B006 plus a three-name B036 is five people, so a two-part prize would require cutting B036 to one name, which would remove the physiology that is the strength of the claim. That is a substantive reason for a single part and not a convenience. On Habener, I would put the limitation in the deliberation record and not in the citation. A citation that names the discoveries and not the individuals would be accurate, but I do not think a citation should hint at who was left out. I would be willing to hear an argument for different wording. On B026, we now agree. If Perlmann and I must declare our past co-authorship again, it concerns dopamine neurons and Nurr1 and has no bearing on any shortlisted name.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius says the BCR-ABL case reads as a drug-development prize with uncredited foundations, though stronger than her ranking implied and not one she would oppose as a second-tier option. She names B031 and B047 as alternatives and asks whether TNF blockade is late recognition or fully mature.
responses.response: Thank you for the candid assessment of B026. I think it is a strong candidate in maturity and impact, but not in attribution, and I no longer place it as a second part. On B031, I agree the Feldmann and Maini pair is tidy and the clinical effect is mature. My reservation is that the cytokine cloning and characterisation and the antibody engineering are outside the credited pair and the principle has been partly absorbed into later cytokine therapies. That is the same discovery-versus-development test applied to GLP-1. I would not choose B031 or B047 over B006 or B042 as my alternatives, but I would not stand in the way of a majority that wanted B031 as a clean second part, and I would want to hear how you see the Eshhar gap in B047 before putting it in my own list.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority on the active peptide can be sustained from the supplied evidence. I have not verified it, and if it cannot be, I would move to Knudsen as the third name.
How the committee should record Habener's absence, and whether a physiology trio is a defensible allocation when a central early contributor is outside the credited names.

Whether the committee prefers to reward the discovery of GLP-1 physiology or the creation of long-acting therapies. My answer favours discovery, but a reasonable member could weigh therapeutic transformation more heavily.
Whether B006 or B042 would be strong enough to justify a second part in a different configuration, given that the three-person limit makes this incompatible with a full GLP-1 trio.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict with any credited name on the shortlist is apparent from my profile. I worked with Paul Greengard as a postdoctoral fellow and have co-authored work with Thomas Perlmann on dopamine neurons, Nurr1 and autophagy. Neither relates to the credited names on the shortlist. Members have disclosed topical proximity of their fields to B042 and B031 and I note it without treating it as a conflict. I have no change to disclose since round 1.
